title: finding: the shipped runtime publish gate already costs linearly in tenant object count — 506 ms per flow publish at 420 objects, before any widening
body:
Restart-when: `npx tsx scripts/bench/runtime-publish-gate.bench.mts` on a then-current `main` reports the real-shape N=420 flow-publish median materially below this band (⇒ some later change reached this door; correct the body and close against a number), OR objectstack cloud has real tenants whose Studio publish latency is a reported symptom

> ## ⛔ Ruled 2026-08-20: **record it, do not fix it.** Maintainer verbatim: 「C 只记录,不修(推荐)」
>
> This card is a **live perf record**, not a work item. Its number was re-measured on 2026-08-20 at **482.78 ms** and is inside the band below. ⛔ Do not scope a narrowing off this card without a new ruling — the measured reason is in "Why the obvious fixes do not reach this door".

Recording a measured fact that has lived only inside a card comment (objectstack-ai/objectstack#4716 comment 5309105113, measured on `origin/main` @ `66beee0f3` by a throwaway harness) so it stops being invisible to every perf listing. Filed unassigned during the 2026-08-18 adjudication of that card (maintainer directed the split package: 「简化开发」→「同意」).

## The measurement

Today's **shipped** gate costs **33.4 ms at 21 objects → 506 ms at 420 objects** per flow publish. The companion per-rule profile shows the bill concentrates in at-gate rules being handed the whole stack: `validateStackExpressions` ≈ 70% of the option-(a) bill, `validateReferenceIntegrity` ≈ 11% — both already on the runtime-publish surface today.

✅ **Re-confirmed twice since, on two later refs and two different machines:**
- 2026-08-19 (PR #9853's reconciliation): 29.6–30.6 ms @21 and 461–485 ms @420 — within ~9%.
- 2026-08-20 (post-#9612): **32.20 ms @21 and 482.78 ms @420** (min 441.98 / max 559.38), via the merged harness. Landing #9612 did **not** move this door.

⚠️ **Parameterisation, which the original wording got slightly wrong:** the cost is linear in the tenant's authored object **SURFACE** — fields, formulas, validation rules, predicates, the expression-bearing keys `validateStackExpressions` walks — **not** its object **count**. Count is a proxy whose constant is set by what the objects contain. At identical N a real-shape stack and a synthetic expression-free one are ~21–26× apart (measured 2026-08-20: real/stub 26.4× @21, 21.4× @420). **Any number quoted from this family must name its stack shape**; not doing so is what once made this card's figure look 16–25× wrong against another correct measurement of a different workload.

## Why it may matter

Flow publish is a user-facing interactive action (Studio designer). Half a second of gate latency at 420 objects is already perceptible, and it grows with exactly the number that grows as a tenant succeeds.

⚠️ **But scope it honestly:** per the maintainer's stated priority, **saving an object/field edit is the high-frequency Studio action while publishing a flow is rare.** The two doors have **disjoint drivers** — the object door is `validateRuleCompilability` at 81.3%, a rule that appears in no profile on this card. ⛔ Every concentration figure here describes **flow publishing** only, and the object door remains **unmeasured**. The better-characterised half is the less important half.

## ⭐ Why the obvious fixes do not reach this door — measured 2026-08-20

Package-narrowing (#9612) requires **two** things, and a tenant-authored overlay stack has **neither**:

1. **A `packageId` on the write.** REST derives it solely from `?package=` (`packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts`, where `'all'`/empty is commented as *"env-local overlay"*), so a Studio publish yields `undefined` and `resolveWritePackageScope` returns at its first guard.
2. **`_packageId` provenance on the stored objects.** `narrowObjectsToPackageClosure`'s limb 2 — `if (typeof owner !== 'string' || owner === '' || owner === OVERLAY_PROVENANCE_SENTINEL) return true;` — **keeps** any object with no provenance, and the real seeded corpus carries **zero**.

⇒ 📌 **Fixing the missing `packageId` (#10063) would not, on its own, buy the saving.** That is the counter-intuitive part and the reason this card stays open: without it, the plumbing fix reads like a latency win and is not one on an unpackaged corpus. Cross-noted on #10063.

**The counterfactual proves the mechanism is sound rather than broken:** on a provenance-stamped seed the shipped deriver narrows 421 objects to 45 (10.7%) and saves **89.5%** (468.10 → 49.36 ms), with the differential verdict semantically unchanged and both positive controls live. The narrowing works; it just cannot reach this corpus.

## ⛔ Fences, carried and still binding

- The **size-threshold** option (skip the gate when N is large) is a deliberate fail-open at scale — the gate stops judging the largest tenants. Same shape as #9798 / #9261 / ADR-0110 D3. ⛔ Not a dev's pick.
- **Caching is refuted on measurement**: #9612 measured snapshot *construction* at 0.001–0.011 ms. 86% of the bill is rules **running**.
- The binding direction if a fix is ever scoped remains the maintainer's input-narrowing ruling (#9612 comment `5339305885`) — which, per the section above, does not reach this door as literally implemented.

## The instrument

```
npx tsx scripts/bench/runtime-publish-gate.bench.mts       # both shapes
npx tsx scripts/bench/runtime-publish-gate.bench.mts --mode package   # the closure counterfactual
```

Re-runnable, states its own timed span, warmup policy and seeded stack shape, prints both shapes, and names the rules it dispatched — so a stale build shows up as a changed rule list rather than as a silently wrong number. It replaces the throwaway harness this card's original reading came from, which was the real problem all along: the number was right, and nobody could re-run it to find that out.
